statement: A top-5 developer weakens or withdraws a published safety-framework commitment, documented by a text diff (calendar 2027)
status_at_phase_end: Resolution window is 2027, but the 2026 base rate is high: at least four Bloc A frontier developers published framework revisions in 2026 that a policy watchdog documented by text diff as removing or softening commitments (pause pledge, numeric thresholds, max-elicitation testing, whistleblower language). Some revisions also added safeguards. Strong prior toward YES for 2027.

items.summary: A top-5 Bloc A developer replaced its if-then scaling policy with v3.0, dropping its implied unilateral pause commitment and demoting higher security standards to 'industry-wide recommendations'; it added public risk reports and a safety roadmap. Executives cited competitors 'blazing ahead'.
items.detail: Anthropic RSP v3.0 (2026-02-24). TIME 'Anthropic drops flagship safety pledge'; GovAI analysis; Midas Project Watchtower 'Major change'.

items.summary: The same developer silently replaced its legally-filed compliance framework, modifying risk thresholds in all categories and narrowing the AI R&D scope to specific fields; prior version no longer published.
items.detail: Anthropic Frontier Compliance Framework update (Watchtower 2026-03-02); question raised over California SB 53 30-day disclosure rule.

items.summary: A Bloc A developer rewrote its frontier framework (v2), broadening triggers and adding a loss-of-control domain and whistleblower protections, while relabelling its top threshold from 'Stop development' to 'Develop with mitigations'. Mixed; mostly a strengthening.

A Bloc A frontier developer rewrote and shortened its framework, removing both quantitative deployment criteria, whistleblower-protection language, the transparency/third-party review section and references to state law.
items.detail: xAI Frontier AI Framework dated 2026-06-30 (Watchtower 2026-07-11, 'Major change'). Note: xAI's top-5 status depends on the site's developer ranking.

items.summary: A top-5 developer's compliance framework raised the bar for activating its automated-AI-R&D tier (requiring a doubling vs both expected and fastest previously observed progress) and dropped 'writing large amounts of critical code' as a named trigger for its misalignment tier.
items.detail: Anthropic FCF update aligned with RSP v3.4 (effective 2026-07-08); Watchtower 2026-07-24.

items.summary: A Bloc A developer renamed and revised its framework (v2.1), adding a loss-of-control category but deleting its maximum-elicitation testing commitment, its numeric cyber threshold and the provisional deployment hold, and softening mitigation-robustness language; several deletions not noted in its changelog.

Watchdog found a Bloc A developer's first full frontier-safety report may fall below its own framework (no named governance function, no explicit acceptable-residual-risk determination) - a compliance gap rather than a text weakening.
items.detail: Google DeepMind Gemini 4 Argon report vs FSF v3.1 (Watchtower 2026-10-13).
